text:
sara: FYI ticket #C-8421 — ACME reports repeated 504s and timeouts on hosted API since 06:00 UTC. They've got a customer-facing outage and escalating to legal. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/C-8421 :cry:

kevin: on it. any obvious deploys at 05:50-06:10?

oncall-bot: deploy:service/hosted-gateway v2.14.1 -> v2.15.0 by dave at 05:57:23 UTC

dave: yep, rolled v2.15.0. rolled forward traffic in 3 waves. no failures reported in CI. watching metrics now.

maria: I'm seeing queue_depth for hosted-gateway spike to ~1.2k at 06:02 UTC, our configured hard_limit is 1000. p95 request latency jumped from 120ms -> 1.9s and p99 -> 5.8s. lots of continuous_batcher backlog.

sara: customer log snippet attached in ticket shows repeated 504s with upstream 'request_queue_timeout'

kevin: can someone pull the continuous_batcher backlog histogram? SQL: SELECT count FROM batcher_backlog WHERE ts > '2026-03-18T05:55:00Z'

maria: result: {"bins": [0-10:1500, 10-50:900, 50-200:320], "median_ms": 34, "tail_ms": 9800} (exported)

dave: looks like tail accumulation. new kernel with batching heuristic seems to favor larger batches when queue depth high -> increases per-request wait. suspect batcher batch_timeout got nudged in v2.15.0

kevin: runbook step A: enable early_reject for tenant acme to prevent deep queuing. Run: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN' https://admin.internal/tenants/acme/actions -d '{"action":"set_throttle","max_queue_depth":700}'

sara: applied early_reject -> max_queue_depth=700 at 06:07:12 UTC. immediate drop in queued requests to ~680. customers still see some 504s but rate down.

maria: also toggled continuous_batcher.batch_timeout back to 12ms (was 40ms in v2.15.0). command: kubectl -n prod set env deploy/continuous-batcher BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=12 --record

dave: restarted 3 batcher pods; they came up 06:11-06:13. tail latency improved after restart. p95 back to ~220ms by 06:18.

support-bot: Posted update to ticket C-8421: "We've applied temporary throttles and reverted batching timeout; mitigation in progress."

kevin: we should also consider temporary model-routing to smaller variant (gpt-small) to reduce token generation time and batch pressure. Can we do that for ACME?

dave: route policy changed for tenant acme -> model=gpt-small at 06:15:40 UTC. traffic shift 40% immediate, 100% by 06:22 with customer consent.

sara: ACME confirms degraded but stable UX at 06:29. legal paused escalation. :relieved:

maria: root cause draft: v2.15.0 changed batching heuristic (prefer max_batch_size vs latency) and defaulted batch_timeout->40ms for NPU path. under sudden ingress spike this allowed queue depth to climb past hard_limit; we hit early_rejection window later causing 504 cascade as inflight requests stayed in batcher for long tails.

kevin: action items:
- revert batching heuristic pr in v2.15.0 (dave)
- add a deploy-time canary metric to assert queue_depth < 0.7*hard_limit (maria)
- improve runbook to auto-enable early_reject at 80% hard_limit (kevin)
- postmortem & customer blameless summary for ACME (sara)

dave: created PR #4092 to revert heuristic. marking P0. ETA for revert -> canary by 09:00 UTC.

eng-runbook: Note: runbook update suggestion: add script /opt/runbook/bin/check_queue.sh that posts to Slack and sets tenant throttle when queue_depth > threshold for >60s. sample: ```#!/bin/bash
Q=$(curl -s http://metrics.internal/queue_depth)
if [ "$Q" -gt 800 ]; then
  curl -s -X POST https://admin.internal/tenants/$1/actions -d '{"action":"set_throttle","max_queue_depth":700}'
fi
```

maria: did we see any auth/billing errors mixed in? logs show a handful of 401s during the surge but mostly from one SDK version; billing flows unaffected.

sara: opened support escalation note and refund hold. keeping ACME channel informed.

kevin: thanks all. follow-ups: dave please tag me on PR; sara keep customer comms. I'll schedule a short incident review at 11:00 UTC.

sara: closing incident thread after postmortem. will file postmortem doc and link here.

support-bot: Incident resolved for tenant ACME; severity lowered to SEV3 at 06:40:12 UTC."
